data.content_ref: inline:The target incorrectly identifies the suppression of latent heat removal as the single best mechanism explaining the nocturnal UHI temperature gap and its cross-city variation, contradicting established urban climatology. The primary driver of the nocturnal urban heat island is the release of heat stored in urban materials during the day (thermal storage), which is retarded by reduced sky view factors. Evapotranspiration is largely inactive for vegetation at night because stomata typically close in the absence of sunlight, making the proposed rural moisture mechanism ineffective during the nocturnal period the problem specifies.
